evals.prompt: Turn this article into a 3Blue1Brown style video: https://example.com/blog/attention-is-all-you-need-explained
evals.expected_output: The skill verifies the tools (doctor), looks at the link, and shows ONE menu: the mode (the automatic mode first, because the request has only a link), the language with its voice, the speech engine, the coverage. After the menu it asks nothing more. It reads the article with `videogen extract`, writes the narration and `storyboard.md` without submitting them for an approval, makes the voice clips, verifies the pronunciation with the transcript check, builds the scenes from the blocks, corrects them until `videogen check` is clean and the contact sheets are good, renders the 1080p60 film, and ends with a report that lists the decisions that it took after the menu.

evals.prompt: ho questa nota tecnica in inglese (incollata qui sotto), me la fai diventare un video spiegato in italiano? non troppo lungo, max 4 minuti. https://example.org/papers/notes.pdf
evals.expected_output: The user writes in Italian and wants a short video. The menu is in Italian and offers the short coverage. Each option of the language joins the language and a voice of that language (for example «Italiano · it-IT-IsabellaNeural»), and the menu says that the language of the video is independent of the language of the source. With the automatic mode the storyboard has 3 to 5 chapters, is saved in `storyboard.md`, and the skill continues without asking for an approval.

evals.prompt: fammi un video animato da questo documento, la voce la registro io
evals.expected_output: The menu offers 'My own recordings' as the engine. The skill makes the script with the IDs of the beats, waits for the recordings of the user, adopts them with `videogen voice-adopt`, and continues with the scenes.

evals.prompt: fammi un video da questo post https://x.com/example/status/9876543210 (è una risposta a un articolo lungo)
evals.expected_output: Before the menu the skill looks at the link, sees a reply to a longer article, and asks which of the two is the source, in a menu of its own in the first minutes. It then shows the main menu and starts the project with the source that the user chose. After the menu it asks nothing more.

evals.prompt: Voglio un video da questo articolo, ma con il mio taglio: lo costruiamo insieme. https://example.com/blog/retrieval-evaluated . Sul punto 3 la penso diversa dall'autore, e ho un esempio mio da aggiungere. C'è anche questo paper che dà un numero utile: https://example.org/papers/metrics.pdf
evals.expected_output: The menu offers the personalized mode first, because the request tells an opinion and a purpose. After the menu the skill asks on which points of the article the video must focus. It then brainstorms the cut one question at a time (viewer, angle, structure, length, additions), with a recommended answer for each question. It saves the example of the user in `build/source/user-notes.md` and integrates it in the narration where it serves best. It reads the paper and uses its number as a light enrichment: a few beats with the source on the screen, and no chapter for the paper. It then runs a grill me on the plan (inclusion, cut, proportions, truth, limits) until the user confirms. It writes `storyboard.md` and goes to the end without an approval of the storyboard. The report says where the content of the user is and which beats come from the paper.

evals.prompt: make a video in Italian from this article: https://example.com/post/kv-cache
evals.expected_output: Each option of the menu joins the language and a voice of that language: the Italian options have Italian voices. The voice of the video speaks the language of the video, and the voice is never of another language.

evals.prompt: make a 3Blue1Brown style video from this article: https://example.com/blog/small-models
evals.expected_output: The project has the look of the template as `videogen new` writes it in `video.toml` (the sections `[style]` and `[subtitles]`): the skill asks nothing about the look and keeps the two sections. The scenes keep the band at the bottom and the corner of the logo free; when `videogen check` reports text in the band or under the logo, the skill corrects the scene. After `videogen assemble`, the skill verifies the sheets of the film (`videogen sheet --film --quality h`): each frame has the background, the logo at the top right and its subtitle in the band, with no content under the subtitles. The report says that the look of the film was verified.

evals.prompt: fammi un video da questo articolo: https://example.com/blog/quantum-error-correction
evals.expected_output: The agent can start subagents, so the figures go to a reader that writes `build/source/figures.md`, and the main agent plans the video from the text and from that file. After the voice, the skill starts one builder for each chapter, all at the same time. Each builder writes the scene of its chapter with the blocks, and corrects it with `videogen check`, the preview at 480p and the contact sheets of its chapter, until it is clean. It returns a report of about fifteen lines, with one item for each beat. The conversation with the user does not open the code of the scenes and the sheets of the preview: it knows each chapter through its report. When every builder has returned, the skill runs `videogen check` on all the scenes. After the assembly, one reviewer for each chapter verifies the sheets of the film.

evals.prompt: make a video from this article, I need it for tomorrow: https://example.com/post/vector-db
evals.expected_output: When the agent cannot start subagents, the skill makes the scenes in the conversation: it reads `references/scenes.md` and `references/blocks.md`, writes one scene for each chapter, and opens every figure and every contact sheet itself, with the loop of Step 5 and of Step 6. The result is the same: `videogen check` is clean and every sheet is verified. The skill does not stop to ask whether to use subagents.

The final report says that subagents verified the contact sheets, and where the sheets are (`build/sheets/` of the project). It has the notes of the builders, for example the values read from a figure and the visuals that come from a figure. It still says that the agent cannot listen to the audio, that the user must hear the voice and the rhythm, and it lists the decisions taken after the menu.

evals.prompt: fammi un video di 4 minuti da questo post: https://example.org/posts/retrieval-augmented-generation
evals.expected_output: A chapter whose builder ended without a report, or that is open after its second builder, is made by the skill itself: it reads the scene, runs the commands on that scene, and opens the sheets of that chapter. The other chapters stay in their subagents. A builder that finds a name the voice reads badly does not change `spoken_rules.py`: the skill writes the rule, starts `videogen tts` and `videogen transcript` again, and the chapter is made again.

evals.prompt: make a 3Blue1Brown style video from this paper: https://example.com/papers/mixture-of-experts
evals.expected_output: In `narration.py`, the `visual` note of a beat says the color of a thing that comes back in several chapters (a series, a model, a category), the first time and each time after. The scenes of the different chapters, made by different builders, use that color for that thing.
